record.original_question: Let Σ be a finite alphabet, let $ be a separator symbol not in Σ, and let string matching mean: given a pattern x and a text y, find all positions where x occurs in y. Does there exist a one-way deterministic finite automaton with finitely many read heads that can perform string matching, equivalently recognize the language {x$uxv | u, x, v ∈ Σ*}, where the substring x that appears before $ occurs again later in the suffix uxv?

evidence.quote: Question 1: Can a one-way multihead dfa perform string matching? More specifically, can such an automaton recognize the language {x$uxv|u, x, v E E*}.
The string matching problem is the following: given two strings, the pattern and the text, find all the occurrences of the pattern in the text.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $\$$ be a separator symbol with $\$\notin\Sigma$. A one-way $k$-head deterministic finite automaton (one-way $k$-head DFA) is a deterministic finite automaton equipped with finitely many ($k$) read-only input heads, each of which can independently move only from left to right over a single input tape (no head may move backward); the automaton accepts or rejects after all heads have reached the right endmarker. Define the string-matching language
$$L = \{\, x\,\$\,u\,x\,v \;:\; x,u,v \in \Sigma^* \,\},$$
i.e., the set of words over $\Sigma\cup\{\$\}$ containing exactly one occurrence of $\$$ such that the prefix $x$ before $\$$ occurs as a (contiguous) factor of the suffix after $\$$.

Question: Does there exist a positive integer $k$ and a one-way $k$-head deterministic finite automaton that recognizes $L$ (equivalently, that performs string matching, identifying all occurrences of a pattern $x$ in a text $uxv$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture of Galil and Seiferas that no one-way k-head DFA can perform string matching was settled in the negative (i.e., string matching cannot be done by any one-way k-head DFA) by T. Jiang and M. Li, "k One-Way Heads Cannot Do String-Matching," J. Comput. System Sci. 1996, building on earlier partial results (Li–Yesha 1986 for k=2; a later paper proving the k=3 case).

status_evidence.title: k One-Way Heads Cannot Do String-Matching (Jiang & Li, JCSS 1996)
status_evidence.snippet: Settles a conjecture raised by Galil and Seiferas, proving that k-head one-way deterministic finite automata cannot perform string-matching for any k.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is resolved: no one-way k-head DFA can recognize the string-matching language.

status_evidence.title: String-matching cannot be done by a two-head one-way DFA (Li & Yesha 1986)
status_evidence.snippet: Earlier result establishing the k=2 case of the Galil–Seiferas conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The k=2 case was solved in 1986.

status_evidence.title: Three One-Way Heads Cannot Do String Matching
status_evidence.snippet: Proves the k=3 case of the Galil–Seiferas conjecture on multihead one-way DFAs.
status_evidence.claim: The k=3 case was proved as an intermediate result.
